title: When the Wolf Breaks Anew
premise: August Underhill, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things until the night the border wards collapse and every star in the sky goes dark. The wards were bound to a king's living memory, and something ancient has been wearing that memory like a crown for thirty years, feeding on it while the realm forgets itself. August must gather the scattered heirs of the old oath-lines and reach the capital before the last dragon-fire — the only flame that can unmake a false crown — gutters out entirely. In the end August learns his own ledgers hold the erased truth of who he was: he chooses truth over the guild's loyalty-oath, burns the false crown with the final dragon-fire at the cost of his swordspeaking voice, and the stars return as the realm begins remembering itself.
about_author: Elodie Eastwick is a former archivist of maritime trade records who swears she once catalogued an invoice for a bottled storm. She writes fantasy from a drafty house on the coast, where her neighbors assume the candle smoke is just her cooking.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: POV August. A quiet night in the Guild of Impossible Things: August audits entries, trades a memory of rain for a jar of borrowed courage, and speaks briefly to his sword out of habit rather than need. The beat is comfort laced with loneliness — a man keeping accounts for a world that no longer believes in oaths.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: POV August. The border wards shatter with a sound like breaking glass across the whole sky; every star vanishes; the guild's impossible inventory goes inert or feral. The Guildmaster hands August a sealed ledger page and orders him south. Beat: dread and duty colliding as comfort dies.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were Holding
chapters.summary: POV August, fleeing the city. He reads the sealed page: the wards were anchored to King Aldric's living memory — meaning the king has none left to give. First glimpse of riders wearing royal black hunting ledger-keepers. Beat: the sick vertigo of learning your life's work was load-bearing.

chapters.title: The Road of Forgotten Names
chapters.summary: POV Sera Vane, a hedge-witch who has forgotten her own mother's face but remembers everyone else's. She finds August half-dead from an ambush and recognizes the guild seal on his satchel. Beat: wary alliance between two people carrying other people's memories.

chapters.title: A Debt Owed in Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: POV Sera. They shelter with the Emberwrights, last keepers of the dragon-fire, dying out in a mountain shrine. Matriarch Ysolde reveals the fire can unmake a false crown but has one guttering flame left — weeks, not months. Beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing His Crown
chapters.summary: POV King Aldric (the true king, imprisoned inside his own body). We see the court through his eyes: a patient, ancient presence ruling in his skin, consuming his memories nightly. Aldric clings to one recollection — a boy with a ledger. Beat: horror rendered intimate and slow.

chapters.title: Heirs of the Broken Oath-Lines
chapters.summary: POV August. In the free town of Marrowgate, August locates two surviving oath-heirs: Tam Broadfoot, a deserter whose oath-line grants unbreakable walls, and Ivet, a child who inherited a line no one can name. Recruiting them means confessing what oaths cost. Beat: reluctant fellowship forged in guilt.

chapters.title: The Guild's Second Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Sera discovers the guild kept a second, hidden ledger recording everything the crown paid to have erased — including entire villages. Her own forgotten mother's name is in it. Beat: betrayal; the institutions August trusted curated the forgetting.

chapters.title: What August Cannot Remember
chapters.summary: POV August. Ambushed by the king's hunters, August's sword refuses to speak for him — and in the silence he realizes gaps riddle his own past. The sealed page hinted: his memories were sold too. Beat: the loyal servant discovering he may be complicit in his own erasure.

chapters.title: Marrowgate Stands
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Royal forces besiege Marrowgate; Tam's wall-oath holds at terrible cost, cracking his bones each hour it endures. August chooses to stay and fight rather than push on, earning the company's trust. Beat: loyalty proven in blood; first real victory.

chapters.title: The Confession of Ysolde Emberwright
chapters.summary: POV Ysolde, in flashback-framed chapters. She reveals the dragon-fire was dimmed deliberately — by the guild, generations ago, as payment for a favor from the thing now wearing the crown. Beat: the full architecture of the betrayal laid bare; August's faith in the guild collapses.

chapters.title: Ivet Dreams the Old Names
chapters.summary: POV Ivet. The child's unnamed oath-line proves to be Remembering: she dreams the names of everyone the crown erased, waking screaming but growing stronger. She names Sera's mother aloud. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose; the party becomes a family.

chapters.title: The Price of the Wall
chapters.summary: POV Tam. The hunters return with a siege-engine that eats oaths. Tam breaks his line deliberately to save the town, losing his gift and nearly his mind. Beat: devastating cost of loyalty; the group carries him onward, diminished but unbroken.

chapters.title: Into the Crown's City
chapters.summary: POV August. The party infiltrates the capital under festival masks on the night of the Unremembering Feast, where citizens celebrate forgetting their dead. August walks streets he suspects he grew up in. Beat: uncanny dread; homecoming without recognition.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Throne
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Guided by Ivet's dreams, they find the vault where the crown stores consumed memories in glass. Sera finds her mother's vial — and August finds a shelf labeled UNDERHILL, holding decades of himself. Beat: temptation; taking memories back might destroy them.

chapters.title: The Boy with the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Aldric. The king, down to his final memory, recognizes August when hunters drag him before the throne-room door: August was the apprentice who witnessed the crowning and was made to forget. Beat: recognition across erasure; the plan's true shape revealed.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Last Invoice
chapters.summary: POV August. The Guildmaster arrives, offering August restoration of all his memories if he surrenders the dragon-fire and lets the crown endure — the guild's survival depends on it. August must choose between the institution that raised him and the truth. Beat: the thematic crux; he signs nothing.

chapters.title: When the Wolf Breaks Anew
chapters.summary: POV August. August breaks his own guild-oath — the wolf of his binding turns on its master — and his sword finally speaks again, with his own stolen voice inside it. The palace erupts into open battle. Beat: catharsis; the title's meaning fulfilled as bondage becomes weapon.

chapters.title: The Guttering Flame
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Fighting through the collapsing feast-hall, the party reaches the throne; Ysolde's heir carries the last dragon-fire and falls mortally wounded passing it on. Ivet carries the flame forward, small and burning. Beat: sacrifice stacking on sacrifice; the clock runs out.

chapters.title: Unbinding the King
chapters.summary: POV Aldric and August, alternating. August uses the archive vials to flood Aldric with returned memory while Ivet sets the dragon-fire against the crown. The thing wearing the king unmakes screaming; Aldric, freed, remembers everything including his captivity. Beat: climax; victory inseparable from pain.

chapters.title: The Stars Return
chapters.summary: POV August. Dawn after: stars rekindle one by one over a capital beginning to weep and remember. August, his swordspeaking voice spent in the unmaking, opens a new ledger — not of debts, but of names being restored. Beat: quiet, earned resolution.

chapters.title: An Entry in the Guild of Possible Things
chapters.summary: POV August, epilogue. Months later, August refounds the guild on honest terms with Sera, the mending Tam, and Ivet the Rememberer; King Aldric visits incognito to open the first entry himself. August writes the first line: 'One star, returned.' Beat: inheritance reclaimed — memory kept, not traded.
